How to grow tomatoes

By Ada Grower &mdash; March 2025

Tomatoes are the classic kitchen-garden crop: fast, generous and forgiving. This guide covers planting, staking and the two diseases every grower meets, with a timeline that works from sowing to harvest in about 90 days.

Getting started

You need seed trays, a warm windowsill and patience. The seeds germinate in 6–10 days at 21 °C — warmer is faster, colder is not.

  • Sow seeds 5 mm deep in fine compost
  • Keep the soil moist, never soggy
  • Pot on when the first true leaves appear
    • one plant per 9 cm pot
    • bury the stem up to the seed leaves

Feeding & watering

Once flowers show, switch to a high-potash feed. A good routine from the Old Farmer's Almanac works for most soils; heavy clay needs less.

Water deeply twice a week; a little every day grows shallow roots and cracked fruit.

Common problems

  1. Blossom end rot — inconsistent watering, add mulch
  2. Blight — remove and burn infected leaves immediately

Planting calendar

MonthTask
MarchSow indoors
MayTransplant outside
JulyFirst harvest

Example row spacing

$ echo "60cm between plants"
90cm between rows

That is everything a first season needs — good luck, and label your varieties, you will not remember which is which by August.
